title: Find the Peaks
summary: Identify the indices of elements in a 0-indexed array that are strictly greater than their neighboring elements, while excluding the first and last elements of the array.
statement: Identify the indices of elements in a 0-indexed array that are strictly greater than their neighboring elements, while excluding the first and last elements of the array.
constraints: A peak index is neither endpoint of the array.
Its value must be strictly greater than both immediate neighbors.
Return all peak indices in increasing order.
reference_solution:
def strict_peak_indices(mountain):
    return [i for i in range(1,len(mountain)-1) if mountain[i]>mountain[i-1] and mountain[i]>mountain[i+1]]
hints: Only immediate neighbors matter for this definition.
Endpoints cannot qualify, so scan indices one through n-2.
Append an index only when both strict greater-than comparisons hold.
The scan examines every and only eligible index, applying the defining condition directly.
editorial: The scan examines every and only eligible index, applying the defining condition directly.

tests.explanation: Index one ties its right neighbor, so there are no strict peaks.
Indices one and three exceed both adjacent values.
